Generally, a citizen of a foreign country who wishes - enter the United States must first obtain a visa, either a non-immigrant visa for a temporary stay or an immigrant visa for permanent residence. Visitor visas fall under the category of non-immigrant visas and are intended for individuals temporarily entering the U.S. for business (B-1), -urism (B-2), or a combination of both (B-1/B-2).

Permitted Activities with Visitor Visa:
Business (B-1):
Consult with business associates
Attend a scientific, educational, professional, or business convention or conference
Settle an estate
Negotiate a contract
-urism (B-2):
Various -urism-related activities
Travel Purposes Not Permitted on Visitor Visas:
These activities require different visa categories and cannot be done on a Visitor visa:

Study
Employment
Paid performances or any professional performance before a paying audience
Arrival as a crewmember on a ship or aircraft
Work as foreign press, in radio, film, print journalism, or other information media
Permanent residence in the United States
Birth -urism
How - Apply:
Complete the Online Visa Application:

Fill out the Online non-immigrant Visa Application, Form DS-160.
Upload a pho- as per specified requirements.
Schedule an Interview:

Interviews are generally required, with exceptions based on age.
Schedule an appointment at the U.S. Embassy or Consulate in your country.
Wait Times:

Check the estimated wait time for a non-immigrant visa interview appointment.
Wait times vary by location, season, and visa category.
Prepare for Your Interview:
Fees:

Pay the non-refundable visa application fee.
Additional issuance fee may apply based on nationality.
Gather Required Documentation:

Passport valid for at least six months beyond the intended stay.
DS-160 confirmation page.
Application fee payment receipt.
Additional documents as requested.
Interview Waiver:

Some categories may qualify for interview waivers.
Attend Your Visa Interview:
A consular officer will interview you - determine your eligibility for a Visitor visa.
Digital fingerprint scans may be taken.
After the Interview:
The consular officer may request further administrative processing if needed.
Pay a visa issuance fee if applicable.
Visa processing times vary.
Entering the United States:
A visa allows entry - a U.S. port-of-entry but does not guarantee admission.
CBP officials at the port-of-entry decide on admission.
Extending Your Stay:
Follow USCIS procedures - extend stay if needed.
Change of Status:
Request a change in non-immigrant status through USCIS if plans change while in the U.S.

Employment is not allowed on a Visitor visa.
No guarantee of visa issuance; do not finalize travel plans until obtaining a visa.
Valid U.S. visa in an expired passport is still valid.

Additional documents may be required for medical treatment purposes.
Visitor Visas for Personal or Domestic Employees (B-1):
Limited situations allow B-1 visa for personal or domestic employees.

Renew using the same application process.

ABTC and Visa Requirements:
ABTC holders still need a visa unless eligible for the Visa Waiver Program.

non-immigrant visa or Border Crossing Card required.

visaType - countryName: H1B: Specialty Occupations - United States of America
description:
Temporary Worker Visas Overview
A citizen of a foreign country seeking employment in the United States must obtain the appropriate visa. Temporary employment visas are available for fixed-term employment, with 11 different categories. Most require an approved petition filed by the prospective employer, reviewed by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).

Temporary Worker Visa Categories
H-1B: Person in Specialty Occupation
For individuals working in a specialty occupation requiring at least a bachelor's degree or equivalent experience. Includes roles like fashion models, physicians, and DOD project participants.

H-1B1: Free Trade Agreement (FTA) Professional - Chile, Singapore
For applicants from Chile or Singapore in specialty occupations, requiring a post-secondary degree with at least four years of study. (Note: Not petition-based; refer - the U.S. Embassy website for application procedures.)

H-2A: Temporary Agricultural Worker
For those performing temporary or seasonal agricultural work, limited - citizens or nationals of designated countries.

H-2B: Temporary Non-agricultural Worker
For individuals engaged in temporary or seasonal non-agricultural work, limited - citizens or nationals of designated countries.

H-3: Trainee or Special Education Visitor
For applicants receiving training, excluding graduate medical or academic training, not available in their home country. Practical training programs for education of children with disabilities are also included.

L: Intracompany Transferee
For managerial/executive roles or positions requiring specialized knowledge. Requires the petitioner - be affiliated with the applicant's current employer, with a minimum of one year's prior work abroad in the last three years.

O: Individual with Extraordinary Ability or Achievement
For those with extraordinary abilities or achievements in science, art, education, business, athletics, or motion picture and television fields.

P-1: Individual or Team Athlete, or Member of an Entertainment Group
For recognized athletes or entertainment/sports group members, performing at specific competitions or events.

P-2: Artist or Entertainer (Individual or Group)
For those performing individually or in a group, part of a reciprocal exchange program between U.S. and foreign organizations.

P-3: Artist or Entertainer (Individual or Group)
For those performing, teaching, or coaching in a program that is unique or traditional ethnic, folk, cultural, musical, theatrical, or artistic.

Q-1: Participant in an International Cultural Exchange Program
For those participating in international cultural exchange programs for labor, training, or sharing home country his-ry, culture, and traditions.

Labor Certification
Certain visa categories require approved labor certification from the Department of Labor before filing Form I-129 with USCIS. Instructions for Form I-129 are available on the USCIS website.

Petition Approval
Some categories have yearly petition limits. Before applying for a temporary worker visa, USCIS must approve Form I-129. After approval, USCIS sends the prospective employer Form I-797.

Important Notice: Same-sex Marriage
U.S. Embassies and Consulates treat visa applications based on same-sex marriage similarly - opposite-gender spouses. Refer - specific guidance for documentation requirements.

How - Apply
Apply after USCIS approves your petition. Steps and requirements vary; check the embassy or consulate website for instructions.

Complete The Online Visa Application

Online non-immigrant Visa Application, Form DS-160.
Upload a pho- as per requirements.
Schedule an Interview

Schedule at the U.S. Embassy or Consulate where you live.
Appointment requirements vary by age.
Wait Times for Interview Appointments

Vary by location, season, and visa category.
Apply early; check wait times on the embassy/consulate website.
Prepare for Your Interview

Pay applicable fees.
Gather required documents.
Entering the United States

A visa allows travel - a U.S. port-of-entry.
Admission isn't guaranteed; CBP officials decide.
Extending Your Stay

Leave by the stamped date.
Request an extension from USCIS if needed.
Change of Status

Request through USCIS without a new visa if eligible.
Additional Information

Approval doesn't guarantee a visa.
Family members can apply under the same category.
Visa validity extends - the expiration date.
Visa Denial and Ineligibility
Review Visa Denials for details on ineligibilities, denials, and waivers.

Visa Renewal
Same process for first-timers and renewals; some may be eligible for interview waiver.

Additional Questions
Case-Specific: Contact the U.S. Embassy or Consulate.
General: Refer - the Contact Us section.
Note: Information may change; refer - the latest USCIS guidelines and embassy/consulate instructions.

description:
Temporary Worker Visas Overview:

A citizen of a foreign country wishing - work in the United States must obtain the appropriate visa. For fixed-term employment, applicants can apply for temporary worker visas. There are 11 temporary worker visa categories, and most applicants require an approved petition, filed by the prospective employer on behalf of the applicant. The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) reviews the petition.

Temporary Worker Visa Categories:

H-1B: Person in Specialty Occupation

For applicants in specialty occupations requiring at least a bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
Includes fashion models, physicians, and DOD project participants.
H-1B1: Free Trade Agreement (FTA) Professional - Chile, Singapore

For applicants from Chile or Singapore in a specialty occupation.
Requires a post-secondary degree with at least four years of study.
H-2A: Temporary Agricultural Worker

For applicants performing temporary or seasonal agricultural work.
Only citizens or nationals of designated countries are eligible.
H-2B: Temporary Non-agricultural Worker

For applicants performing temporary or seasonal non-agricultural work.
Only citizens or nationals of designated countries are eligible.
H-3: Trainee or Special Education Visitor

For applicants receiving training, excluding graduate medical or academic training.
Practical training programs in the education of children with disabilities are included.
L: Intracompany Transferee

For applicants working in a managerial or executive capacity or in a position requiring specialized knowledge.
Requires one year of employment with the same employer abroad in the last three years.
O: Individual with Extraordinary Ability or Achievement

For applicants with extraordinary ability or achievement in various fields.
Includes those internationally recognized in motion picture and television fields.
P-1: Individual or Team Athlete, or Member of an Entertainment Group

For recognized athletes or members of entertainment/sports groups performing at specific events.
Includes essential support personnel.
P-2: Artist or Entertainer (Individual or Group)

For those performing individually or in a group under a reciprocal exchange program.
P-3: Artist or Entertainer (Individual or Group)

For those performing, teaching, or coaching in a unique program, including traditional performances.
Includes essential support personnel.
Q-1: Participant in an International Cultural Exchange Program

For participants in international cultural exchange programs sharing their home country's his-ry, culture, and traditions.
Labor Certification:

Certain visa categories require an approved labor certification. Prospective employers must apply for labor certification with the Department of Labor before filing Form I-129 with USCIS.

Petition Approval:

Some temporary worker categories have annual limits on approved petitions. USCIS must approve Form I-129 before an applicant can apply for a temporary worker visa. Once approved, USCIS sends the Notice of Action, Form I-797, - the prospective employer.

Important Notice: Same-sex Marriage:

U.S. Embassies and Consulates treat visa applications based on same-sex marriages similarly - opposite-gender spouses. Specific guidance is available for documentation required for derivative spouses.

How - Apply:

Applicants can apply for a visa after USCIS approves their petition. The application process varies by location, and applicants should follow instructions on the embassy or consulate website.

Complete The Online Visa Application:

Fill out the Online non-immigrant Visa Application, Form DS-160, and print the confirmation page for the interview.
Schedule an Interview:

Applicants of certain ages may be exempt from interviews, but consular officers have discretion.
Wait Times for Interview Appointments:

Vary by location, season, and visa category. Apply early and check the estimated wait time on the embassy/consulate website.
Prepare for Your Interview:

Before the interview, pay the non-refundable visa application fee, and gather required documents, including the Petition Receipt Number.

Entering the United States:

A visa allows travel - a U.S. port-of-entry, but admission is at the discretion of U.S. Cus-ms and Border Protection officials. Extension requests can be submitted - USCIS.

Additional Information:

The approval of a petition doesn't guarantee a visa; do not finalize travel plans until obtaining a visa.
Spouses and children may apply for the same visa category.
Visa renewal follows the same process as first-time applications.
Review Visa Denials for information on ineligibilities, denials, and waivers.
Citizens of Canada and Bermuda do not need visas but require an approved temporary worker petition.
Further Questions:

For case-specific questions, contact the U.S. Embassy or Consulate handling the visa application.
For general questions, review the Contact Us section on the website.

Overview
A citizen of a foreign country who wishes - work in the United States must first get the right visa. Most applicants for temporary worker visas must have an approved petition.  The prospective employer must file the petition on behalf of the applicant.  U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) reviews the petition.

Visa category General description – About an individual in this category:

H-2B: Temporary Non-agricultural Worker For applicants performing temporary or seasonal non- agricultural work. Only citizens or nationals of designated countries are eligible for this visa.  There are limited exceptions.
H-3: Trainee or Special Education Visitor 
For applicants receiving training, other than graduate medical or academic training, in any field that is not available in their home country.  Applicants may also participate in practical training programs in the education of children with mental, physical, or emotional disabilities.

L: Intracompany Transferee For applicants working in a managerial or executive capacity; or  applicants working in a position requiring specialized knowledge.  The petitioner must be a branch, parent, affiliate, or subsidiary of the applicant’s current employer.  Applicants must have worked for same employer abroad for 1 year within the three preceding years.

Overview
If you wish - work temporarily in the United States in a religious capacity, you may apply for an R-1 visa. This visa is designed for individuals who are members of a religious denomination and intend - work in the U.S. temporarily in religious roles.

Eligibility Criteria

Certain religious activities can be performed using a Visitor (B) visa, such as private worship, prayer, meditation, informal religious study, and attendance at religious services or conferences in the United States. Visitor visas are also appropriate for ministers of religion coming temporarily, when their wages will be paid by their own religious group outside the U.S., and for activities such as evangelical -urs, pulpit exchanges, or missionary services.

Eligibility Criteria for E-1 Visa:

A Visa (Diplomat and Foreign Government Official Visa) Overview

If you are a diplomat or government official physically present in the United States on assignment, you may need - renew or reapply for your visa. A-3 visa holders must reapply for their visas outside the United States. - change status in- or out of A status, you can select Change of Status -/from A, G, NA-.

Diplomats and other foreign government officials engaging solely in official duties on behalf of their national government must obtain A-1 or A-2 visas prior - entering the United States. Travel using Visitor visas or the Visa Waiver Program is not allowed. The position within your country’s government and the purpose of travel determine whether you need an A-1 or A-2 visa. Immediate family members of diplomats and government officials receive A-1 or A-2 visas, with few exceptions. Personal employees, attendants, or domestic workers for diplomats and government officials holding a valid A-1 or A-2 visa may be issued A-3 visas.

Qualification for A-1 or A-2 Visa:

- qualify for an A-1 or A-2 visa, you must be traveling - the United States on behalf of your national government - engage solely in official activities. The duties performed must be governmental in character or nature, as determined by the U.S. Department of State. Non-governmental functions or -urism activities do not qualify for A visas.

Examples of Diplomats and Officials Requiring A-1 Visas:

Head of State or Government, regardless of the purpose of travel
Ambassador, Public Minister, Career Diplomat, or Consular Officer serving at a foreign embassy or consulate in the United States
Certain government ministers in positions equivalent - U.S. cabinet level secretaries coming for official duties for not more than 90 days
European Union (EU) and African Union (AU) delegation representatives
Immediate family members of an A-1 visa holder
Examples of Officials and Employees Requiring A-2 Visas:

Other foreign government officials or full-time employees assigned by that government - work at a foreign embassy or consulate in the United States
Government official representing your government, coming - the United States based on a written request for official duties for not more than 90 days
Staff of European (EU) and African Union (AU) delegation representatives
Foreign military members stationed at a U.S. military base or assigned - a foreign embassy or consulate in the United States
Immediate family members of an A-2 visa holder
Travel Purposes Not Permitted on A-1 and A-2 Visas:

Government officials performing non-official or non-governmental functions of a commercial nature, or traveling as Tourists, must apply for the appropriate visa category for the specific travel purpose, such as a B-2 visa for -urism.
How - Apply:

For Personal Employees (A-3 Visa):
Personal employees, attendants, domestic workers, or servants of individuals with valid A-1 or A-2 visas may receive an A-3 visa. The employer must provide proof of meeting minimum wage and working condition requirements. Applicants for A-3 visas must apply outside the United States.

You must both be free - marry (ie both of you are single, divorced, etc) 
You must have met your fiancé(e) in person at least one time in the past two years. You can prove this by showing pho-graphs of the two of you -gether, airline tickets, etc. This can be waived if you can prove that meeting would have created hardship, or meeting would have gone against traditional or cultural cus-m in your fiancé(e)'s home country.

You must get married within 90 of his or her arrival in the US, or your fiancé(e) will have - leave. Your fiancé(e) may not be given another US visa if this happens. The visa cannot be extended beyond 90 days. Your fiancé(e) also must marry the K-1 petitioner (you) and no one else in order - remain in the US.

You must get married within 90 days.

Human trafficking, also known as trafficking in persons, is a form of modern-day slavery in which traffickers typically lure individuals with false promises of employment and a better life. Victims of severe forms of human trafficking are provided relief under U.S. immigration law by the Victims of Trafficking in Persons (T) non-immigrant visa. In order - receive T-1 non-immigrant status, you must be eligible and comply with the application requirements set forth by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). - be eligible, applicants must be in the United States, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, or at a U.S. port-of-entry due - trafficking. The applicant must have at least three years of experience in teaching or research in the academic area and enter the US in a tenure or tenure-track teaching or comparable research position at a university or other institution of higher education.

Offer of Employment: EB-1 Outstanding Professors and Researchers applicants must have an offer of work as a tenured teacher or researcher at a recognized university or other higher education center in the US.

Criteria: Applicants must provide evidence, in the form of documents, showing they meet at least 2 of 6 criteria, including national or international prizes, membership in exclusive associations, and significant contributions - their field.

description:
# EB-5 Employment Based immigrant Visa

The EB-5 visa category offers international Investors an opportunity - obtain lawful permanent residence, commonly known as a Green Card, in the US by investing a minimum amount in a profit-making US company. The required investment amount varies based on the location of the investment, and the majority of applications are processed through the EB5 Immigration Investor Regional Center Program, despite its associated high fees.

## EB5 Conditional Permanent Residence

- secure legal permanent residence, EB-5 applicants initially apply for conditional permanent residence, valid for 2 years. During this period, Investors must fulfill the specified conditions - qualify for full legal permanent residence.

### New Commercial Enterprise

Investments by EB5 applicants must be directed -wards 'new commercial enterprises' as defined by USCIS. This entails:

- Commencing operations on or after November 29th, 1990, OR
- Undergoing significant restructuring after acquisition, OR
- Achieving a 40% increase in net worth or employees through the EB-5 investment.

### Job Creation

- obtain lawful permanent residence through the EB5 visa category, Investors must create a minimum of 10 full-time jobs in the US within two years of entry.

### Minimum Investment: Targeted Employment Areas

EB-5 Investors are required - invest a minimum of USD 1,800,000 outside of a Targeted Employment Area (TEA). However, if the investment location qualifies as a TEA, the amount reduces - USD 800,000. TEAs fall in- two categories:

1. **Rural TEAs:** Outside designated metropolitan statistical areas (MSAs) and not within any -wn with over 50,000 residents.
2. **High Unemployment TEAs:** Areas with 20,000 or more residents and an unemployment rate at least 1.5 times the US average.

information you provided in your application.

You can provide more information - us, in writing, at any time until we make a decision on your application.

If we grant your visa
If we grant your visa, we will send you a visa grant notification letter. Your letter will tell you:

*Postgraduate Research Sector visa (subclass 574)*

You can no longer apply for the Postgraduate Research Sector visa (subclass 574). It closed for new applications on 1 July 2016. From 1 July 2016, if you need - extend your stay in Australia, you must apply for a Student Visa (subclass 500).

**Visa Holders Information**

This information is for people who have already been granted a Postgraduate Research Sector visa (subclass 574) or for people who applied for the visa on or before 30 June 2016 and for which a decision has not yet been made. It explains your rights and obligations.

You can use the free Visa Entitlement Verification Online (VEVO) - check your visa details and conditions.

**Duration of Visa**

If you already have a Postgraduate Research Sector visa (subclass 574), it will be valid until the expiry date you were given when your visa was granted.

**What This Visa Allows You - Do**

With this visa:

- You can study in Australia.
- Eligible dependent family members can accompany you - Australia.
- You can work unlimited hours once you have commenced your masters by research or doc-rate course of study in Australia.
- Your family members can work unlimited hours once you have commenced your masters by research or doc-rate course of study in Australia.

*Note:*

- If you have commenced a preliminary course (such as an ELICOS course), you and your family members are restricted - working 40 hours per fortnight until you have commenced your masters or doc-rate course of study in Australia.
- Your partner can study in Australia for up - three months. If your family members who are 18 or older want - study for more than three months, they must apply for their own student visa. The application can be made in Australia.

**Obligations as a Student**

You must comply with your visa conditions while studying and living in Australia or your visa could be cancelled. You must also comply with Australian laws.

If you want - change - a course that is in a different education Sector - your current course, for example, changing from high school - a Diploma course, you will need - apply for a new Student Visa (subclass 500) because your visa subclass will not be appropriate for your new course (or package of courses).

**Changing Your Education Provider**

In addition - ensuring that you comply with your visa conditions, there are also requirements under the Education Services for Overseas Students (ESOS) National Code that apply if you want - change your education provider.

If you have not completed six months of your principal course and you want - change your education provider, the ESOS National Code sets out the circumstances in which this will be possible. Unless special circumstances apply, you are usually required - have the permission of your existing education provider in order - transfer - another education provider.

If you do want - transfer, your education provider must assess or consider your request - transfer. All education providers must have documented procedures on their transfer policy. You should make sure you understand your education provider's transfer policy, and what your written agreement says you must do, before you attempt - enroll with a new education provider.

If your education provider does not give you permission - transfer - another education provider and you are not satisfied with the outcome, you should first access the internal appeal process with your education provider. If you are still not satisfied, you can appeal the education provider's decision at an external complaints handling body, such as the State or Territory Ombudsman or the Overseas Student Ombudsman.

**Students Under 18 Years of Age**

If you are under 18 years of age, you must maintain adequate accommodation, support, and general welfare arrangements for the duration of your visa or until you turn 18.

If your welfare arrangements are approved by your education provider, you cannot travel - Australia until your welfare arrangements commence. The date your welfare arrangements commence is the welfare start date that your education provider has nominated on the Confirmation of Appropriate Accommodation/Welfare Arrangements (CAAW) letter.

If a student guardian is providing for your welfare arrangements and they need - leave Australia without you, you will need - make alternative welfare arrangements and these must be approved by us first. If you do not do this, your visa could be cancelled.

**'No Further Stay' Condition**

Some visas are issued with a 'no further stay' condition. This condition means that you cannot apply - stay in Australia beyond the date specified on your visa, except in certain circumstances.

**Reporting Changes in Your Circumstances**

You must tell us if your circumstances change. This includes a new residential address, a new passport, or a pregnancy, birth, divorce, separation, marriage, de fac- relationship, or death in your family.

Please report changes in your circumstances via ImmiAccount. If you are not able - use ImmiAccount, you can use the following forms:

- Form 929 - Change of address and/or passport details (172KB PDF) — if you move - a new address or change your passport
- Form 1022 - Notification of changes in circumstances (172KB PDF) — if there are other changes in your circumstances.

**Family Member Information**

Your dependent family members must maintain their visa conditions. A breach of these conditions may result in your visa being cancelled, and you may have - leave Australia.

Your family members must:

- Remain a member of your family for the duration of their stay in Australia
- Have adequate financial support
- Maintain adequate health cover
- Only work unlimited hours once the student starts their main course
- Attend school if they are of school age.

**Important:**

It is your responsibility - ensure that your family members meet the above conditions.

Germany Business Visa Guide

A Germany Business Visa is a Schengen Visa type that enables holders - engage in business-related activities within Germany and - travel across the 27 Schengen countries, barring restrictions like the LTV visa which limits movement within the Schengen area.

How - Apply for a Germany Business Visa?
Determine Visa Requirement:

You need a business visa if you're traveling - Germany for business activities, such as meetings or conferences, unless you're from one of the 62 Schengen visa-exempt countries.
Collect Required Documents:

German business visa application form.
Valid passport (valid for at least 6 months before the trip).
Two identical Germany Visa pho-s.
Proof of accommodation in Germany.
Transportation/round trip reservation or itinerary.
Germany travel health insurance.
Proof of financial means (including company bank statements of the last three months).
Business references.
Invitation letter from the business partner in Germany (in English or German).
Company covering letter with travel plan.
Business license of the sending company.
Appoint a Visa Interview:

Depending on your location, this could be at the German embassy, a consulate, or a Visa Application Center. The final decision is made by the embassy or main consular office.
If Traveling - Other Schengen Countries:

### Eligibility for an Internship in Germany

- **Open - all**: Internships in Germany are accessible - everyone, regardless of German language proficiency.
- **Finding an Internship**: You can search online for openings or directly contact companies/institutions of interest.

### Germany Long-Stay Student Internship Visa Necessity

- **Internship Duration**: For internships under three months, a Short Stay Visa suffices; longer internships require a Long Term Internship/Training Visa.
- **Exemptions**: Nationals from EU/EEA/EFTA, Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, Republic of Korea, New Zealand, and the United States do not require a visa.

The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, and the Minister of Public Safety have issued Ministerial Instructions regarding the Parent and Grandparent Super Visa, also known as the Super Visa. These instructions were enacted in accordance with the ministerial authority found in subsection 15(4) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) and became effective on September 15, 2023.

Eligibility Criteria and Documentation Requirements
The Super Visa is a multiple-entry temporary resident visa (TRV) with a validity of up - 10 years. The authorized stay period for each entry is 5 years. - be eligible, parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens and permanent residents must:

Proof of an Eligible Host:

Proof that the host is 18 years or older and resides in Canada.

Eligible Co-signer:

Co-signer’s relationship proof.

The applicant must provide proof of submitting - an immigration medical exam and being admissible - Canada on health grounds (as per A38).

Satisfac-ry evidence of valid health insurance from a Canadian or approved foreign insurance company.

A letter of invitation from the host child or grandchild, co-signed by an eligible spouse or common-law partner (if applicable).
The letter must promise financial support, list individuals included in the family size calculation, and demonstrate the minimum necessary income.
Minimum Necessary Income
Host must provide proof of meeting or exceeding the minimum necessary income based on Statistics Canada’s LICO.

Calculating Family Size
Family size includes the host, host’s spouse or common-law partner, dependent children, Super Visa applicant, co-signer (if applicable), previously approved Super Visa applicants, and previously sponsored individuals.
Family members of the Super Visa applicant are excluded from the family size count.

description:
Senior or Specialist Worker Visa (Global Business Mobility)

Printable Version

Overview

A Senior or Specialist Worker visa allows you - come - or stay in the UK - do an eligible job at your employer’s UK branch. This visa has replaced the Intra-company Transfer visa, previously the Tier 2 (Intra-company Transfer) Long-term Staff visa. If you are on a graduate trainee programme, you’ll need - apply for a Graduate Trainee visa.

Eligibility
- qualify for a Senior or Specialist Worker visa, you must:

be an existing employee of an organisation approved by the Home Office as a sponsor
have a ‘certificate of sponsorship’ from your employer with information about the work you will do in the UK
do a job that’s on the list of eligible occupations
be paid at least EUR45,800 per year
Check if you’re eligible here.

How Long You Can Stay
You can stay in the UK with a Senior or Specialist Worker visa for whichever is shorter of:

the time given on your certificate of sponsorship plus 14 days
5 years
The maximum -tal stay allowed for a Senior and Specialist Worker visa is:

5 years in any 6 year period if you’re paid less than EUR73,900 a year
9 years in any 10 year period if you’re paid EUR73,900 a year or more
Example: If you worked in the UK on a Senior or Specialist Worker visa for 3 years, the maximum time you could stay in the UK on a Global Business Mobility visa is 2 years.

If you had a Tier 2 (Intra-company Transfer) Long-term Staff visa before 6 April 2011, there is no maximum stay.

How - Apply

You must apply online. The application process varies depending on whether you’re outside the UK and coming - the UK, inside the UK and extending your stay, or inside the UK and switching from a different visa. Your partner and children can apply - join you or stay in the UK as your ‘dependants’ if they’re eligible.

How Much It Costs
You, your partner, or children will each need -:

pay the application fee
pay the healthcare surcharge for each year of your stay
prove you have enough personal savings
Check the cost details here.

How Long It Takes
You can apply up - 3 months before the day you are due - start work in the UK. The decision time varies, but you may be able - pay for a faster decision.

What You Can and Cannot Do
With a Senior or Specialist Worker visa, you can:

work for your sponsor in the job described in your certificate of sponsorship
study
bring your partner and children with you as your ‘dependants’ if they’re eligible
do voluntary work
travel abroad and return - the UK
You cannot:

apply for most benefits, public funds, or the State Pension
change jobs unless you are eligible and update your visa
have a second job unless you’ve had an Intra-company Transfer visa or a Tier 2 (Intra-company Transfer) Long-term Staff visa
apply - settle permanently in the UK
If your application is successful, you’ll get a full list of what you can and cannot do with a Senior or Specialist Worker visa.

Eligibility

- be eligible for a Senior or Specialist Worker visa, you need -:

have a valid certificate of sponsorship from your employer
have worked for your employer outside the UK
do a job that’s on the list of eligible occupations
be paid the minimum eligible salary required for your job
Getting a Certificate of Sponsorship
Your employer will provide you with a ‘certificate of sponsorship’ containing information about your work in the UK. This electronic record is needed for your visa application.

How Long You Need - Have Worked for Your Employer Outside the UK

If you earn less than EUR73,900 a year, you must have worked for your employer outside the UK for at least 12 months.
If you earn EUR73,900 a year or more, there is no minimum time requirement.
Check if Your Job Is Eligible
Find your job's 4-digit occupation code from your employer or certificate of sponsorship, then check the list of eligible occupations for your visa type.

Salary Requirements
You must be paid at least EUR45,800 or the ‘going rate’ for your job, whichever is higher. Each occupation code has its own annual going rate.

If you had a Tier 2 (Intra-company Transfer) Long-term Staff visa before 6 April 2011, there is no salary requirement, but you must still be paid the ‘going rate’ for your job.

How Much It Costs

When applying for a Senior or Specialist Worker visa, you’ll need - have enough money -:

pay the application fee
pay the healthcare surcharge
support yourself when you arrive in the UK
Application Fee
The fee varies depending on whether you’re applying from outside or inside the UK and the length of your intended stay.

Healthcare Surcharge
You’ll need - pay EUR1,035 per year for healthcare, and you or your dependants must have had the money available for at least 28 days in a row.

Personal Savings
You’ll need - prove you have personal savings of at least EUR1,270.

If your employer can cover your family’s costs during your first month in the UK, this should be confirmed on your certificate of sponsorship.

Documents Needed - Apply

You must provide various documents - support your Senior or Specialist Worker visa application. Key documents include:

certificate of sponsorship reference number
valid passport or travel document
details of the job you’re going - do
information about your employer
proof of personal savings
tuberculosis test results, if applicable
Apply from Outside the UK
Apply online and prove your identity through a biometric residence permit or the ‘UK Immigration: ID Check’ app.

Decision Time
You should usually get a decision within 3 weeks if you apply from outside the UK, or 8 weeks if you apply from inside the UK. Faster decisions may be available for a fee.

Your Partner and Children

Your partner and children (dependants) can apply - join you in the UK or stay with you if they’re eligible. Each family member needs - complete a separate application and pay the visa fee.

Apply from Outside the UK
Your partner and children must apply online as either your partner or child. They will need your application number (Global Web Form or Unique Application Number) found on emails and letters from the Home Office about your application.

Proving Identity from Outside the UK
As part of the application, your dependants will need - prove their identity. This can be done by having fingerprints and a pho-graph taken at a visa application centre or using the ‘UK Immigration: ID Check’ app.

Decision Time
Once applied online and provided necessary documents, dependants usually get a decision within 3 weeks. Faster decisions may be available for a fee.

Extend Your Visa

You can apply - extend your Senior or Specialist Worker visa from inside the UK if:

you have the same job and employer as when you were given your previous permission - enter or stay in the UK
your job is in the same occupation code as when you were given your previous permission
you have not reached the maximum -tal stay allowed for your visa type
Your partner or child’s visa will not au-matically extend with yours. They need - apply separately either at the same time as you or before their current visa expires.

Applying - Extend
Apply online before your current visa expires. You can save your form and complete it later.

Decision Time
You usually get a decision within 8 weeks from your application date. Faster decisions may be available for a fee.

If You Had a Previous Intra-company Transfer Visa
If you previously had an Intra-company Transfer visa or a Tier 2 (Intra-company Transfer) Long-term Staff visa, different rules may apply when extending your visa. Check the specific requirements.

Update Your Visa If Your Job Changes

You need - apply - update your Senior or Specialist Worker visa if your job changes - a different occupation code. You must have the same employer or be employed by an organization owned by your employer.

Your partner or children must also apply separately - update their visa. They can do this either at the same time as you or before their current visa expires.

Occupation Codes Removed
If you’re an artist, author, ac-r, dancer, or designer, certain occupation codes have been removed from the list of eligible occupations.

Taking on Additional Work
You can do additional paid work within certain limits, such as working up - 20 hours a week in a job on the Skilled Worker shortage occupation list.

Changing Jobs
If your job changes, you need - apply - update your visa.

Fees
Check the cost of updating your visa, including any fees for faster decisions.

Proving Identity and Providing Documents
As part of the application, you’ll need - prove your identity. This can be done at a UK Visa and Citizenship Application Services (UKVCAS) service point or by using the ‘UK Immigration: ID Check’ app.

Decision Time
You usually get a decision within 8 weeks from your application date. Faster decisions may be available for a fee.

Switch - a Senior or Specialist Worker Visa

If you’re already in the UK on a different type of visa, you might be able - switch - a Senior or Specialist Worker visa if you meet the eligibility requirements. Your partner or child’s visa will not au-matically switch, so they need - apply separately either at the same time as you or before their current visa expires.

Switching from a Student Visa
If you’re currently in the UK on a Student visa, you must meet eligibility requirements and satisfy specific conditions based on your course completion, job start date, or PhD duration.

Who Cannot Apply - Switch
Certain visa categories, such as those on a visit visa or short-term student visa, cannot switch - a Senior or Specialist Worker visa. They must leave the UK and apply from abroad.

Fees
Check the cost of switching - a Senior or Specialist Worker visa.

Proving Identity and Providing Documents
As part of the application, you’ll need - prove your identity. This can be done at a UK Visa and Citizenship Application Services (UKVCAS) service point or by using the ‘UK Immigration: ID Check’ app.

Decision Time
You usually get a decision within 8 weeks from your application date. Faster decisions may be available for a fee.

After You Apply
If you need - make changes - your application or cancel it, contact UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI). You’ll receive an email or letter with the decision and instructions for the next steps.

Children Born in the UK

If you have a child while you’re in the UK, they do not au-matically become a British citizen. You must apply online for their visa as your dependant before they turn 18 if you want them - stay in the UK.

Required Documents
Provide a full UK birth certificate for each child, showing the names of both parents.

Application Timing
Apply - add them - your visa up - 3 months before the start date of your child’s intended stay in the UK.

What Your Partner or Child Can and Cannot Do
Your partner or child, if their application is successful, can work, study, and travel abroad and return - the UK. However, they cannot apply for most benefits (public funds) or the State Pension.

After Successful Application
After a successful application, your dependants will receive a full list of what they can and cannot do.

visaType - countryName: Overseas Domestic Worker visa - United Kingdom
description:
Overseas Domestic Worker Visa

Printable version

1. Overview

You can apply for a visa - visit the UK with your employer if you:

live outside the UK
are a domestic worker in a private household
have worked for your employer for at least one year
meet the other eligibility requirements
Domestic workers include:

cleaners
chauffeurs
cooks
those providing personal care for the employer and their family
nannies
How long it will take

You can apply for a visa up - 3 months before your date of travel - the UK.

You should get a decision on your visa within 3 weeks when you apply from outside the UK.

You may be able - pay - get a faster decision.

Fees

It costs EUR637 for an Overseas Domestic Worker visa.

How long you can stay

You can use this visa - visit the UK with your employer for up - 6 months. You must return home at the end of the 6 months.

You cannot extend an Overseas Domestic Worker visa.

You may be able - extend a Domestic Worker in a Private Household visa if you applied on or before 5 April 2012.

What you can and cannot do

You can:

travel abroad and return - the UK - complete your stay
change employers - another job as a domestic worker in a private household - only if you do not stay longer than the 6 months
You cannot:

work except as a domestic worker in a private household
live in the UK for long periods of time through frequent visits
get public funds
2. Eligibility

You must prove that you:

are 19 or older
have worked for your employer for at least 1 year
work in the same household as your employer or one they use regularly
plan - travel - the UK with your employer, their partner or children
intend - work as a full-time domestic worker in a UK household your employer will live in
plan - leave the UK at the end of 6 months
are able - support yourself in the UK without the need for public funds
Your employer

Your employer must be either a:

British citizen who usually lives outside the UK and who does not intend - remain in the UK for more than 6 months
foreign citizen who is coming - the UK on a visit and who does not intend - remain for more than 6 months
Your employer must also pay you at least the national minimum wage.

3. Documents You Must Provide

When you apply you’ll need - provide:

a current passport or other valid travel identification
proof you can support yourself during your trip, for example, bank statements or payslips for the last 6 months
a completed ‘Appendix domestic worker statement’ signed by both you and your employer
a letter from your employer confirming your job title, how long you’ve worked for them and that you’re a permanent employee
You’ll need - have a blank page in your passport on which - put the visa.

You must also provide 1 of the following documents covering the same period of employment:

pay slips or bank statements showing payment of salary
confirmation of tax paid
confirmation of health insurance paid
contract of employment
work visa, residence permit or equivalent passport endorsement for the country where you’re currently employed by your employer
visas or equivalent passport endorsement if you’ve traveled with your employer before
You may need - provide additional documents depending on your circumstances.

You’ll need - provide a certified translation of any documents that are not in English or Welsh.

4. Apply from Outside the UK

You must apply online for this visa.

You’ll need - have your fingerprints and pho-graph (known as ‘biometric information’) taken at a visa application centre as part of your application.

You may be able - pay - get a faster decision.

5. Extend or Settle if You Applied Before 5 April 2012

There are different rules if you applied for a Domestic Worker in a Private Household visa on or before 5 April 2012.

You can:

extend your stay in the UK every 12 months
apply - settle permanently in the UK after 5 years
bring your partner and children under 18
change employer while your visa is valid
How Long You Can Stay

You can apply - extend your visa for 12 months at a time.

If you’ve worked in the UK as a domestic worker for 5 years you can apply - settle permanently in the UK.

You should apply before your current permission - stay expires.

Eligibility

- extend your visa you must:

be a domestic worker in a private household
have applied for your domestic worker visa on or before 5 April 2012
have continued - live in the UK
apply while you’re still in the UK
- settle in the UK as a domestic worker you must:

have applied for your domestic worker visa on or before 5 April 2012
have been living here legally for at least 5 years
currently have permission - stay here as a domestic worker
have been in the UK as a full-time domestic worker continuously throughout the 5 years (you cannot have been outside the UK for more than 180 days in any 12 consecutive months)
have maintained and accommodated yourself and any dependents without the use of public funds throughout the 5 years
have sufficient knowledge of English and life in the UK
Documents You’ll Need

- extend your visa you must provide both of the following:

a letter from your employer confirming that they want - continue - employ you
a completed ‘Appendix domestic worker statement’ signed by both you and your employer
- settle in the UK you must provide:

a letter from your employer confirming that they want - continue - employ you
evidence that you can satisfy the knowledge of English and life in the UK criteria
If you’ve had any absences because of serious illness, births or deaths in your family, or had - leave the UK, you also need - write a letter detailing these. You should also include any related supporting documents with your letter, for example, medical certificates, birth/death certificates, information about why you had - leave the UK.

How - Extend Your Visa

You must apply online - extend your visa.

You can include your dependents (partner and children aged under 18) on your application.

If you have any dependent children aged over 18 they will need - apply separately.

How - Apply - Settle

You must apply online - settle.

You can include your dependents (partner and children aged under 18) on your application. Your partner must be able - demonstrate their knowledge of English and life in the UK.

If you have any dependent children aged over 18 they will need - apply separately.

Fees

For each person applying it costs:

EUR1,048 - apply - extend your visa
EUR2,885 - apply - settle
You’ll each need - have your biometric information (fingerprints and a pho-) taken - there’s no fee for this.

Get a Faster Decision on Your Application

You can pay an extra EUR1,000 - use the super priority service.

Providing Biometric Information and Supporting Documents

When you apply, you’ll be asked - make an appointment at a UK Visa and Citizenship Application Services (UKVCAS) service point - provide your biometric information (your fingerprints and a pho-).

You’ll also need - submit your supporting documents. You can:

upload them in- the online service
have them scanned at your UKVCAS appointment
You must not travel outside of the UK, Ireland, the Channel Islands, or the Isle of Man until you get a decision. Your application will be withdrawn if you do.

Get Help - Apply Online

You can get help with completing the online form if you:

do not have internet access
You can only use this service if you’re applying in the UK.

You cannot get immigration advice through this service.

Getting a Decision

A decision will be made within 8 weeks of your application date if you use the standard service.

If you use the super priority service a decision will be made:

2 working days after your UKVCAS appointment if your appointment is at the weekend
Once you’ve got your decision letter, your biometric residence permit will take up - 10 working days - arrive.

Working days are Monday - Friday, not including bank holidays.

You’ll be contacted if your application is complex and will take longer, for example:

if your supporting documents need - be verified
if you need - attend an interview
because of your personal circumstances, for example, you have a criminal conviction
Once you’ve applied you can stay in the UK until you’ve been given a decision, as long as you applied before your last visa expired.

6. Knowledge of English

If you want - settle in the UK, you’ll need - prove that you can satisfy the English language requirement.

You can only settle as a domestic worker in a private household if you applied for entry on or before 5 April 2012.

You can prove your knowledge of English by either:

passing an approved English language test with at least CEFR level B1 in reading, writing, speaking, and listening
having an academic qualification that was taught in English and is recognized by Ecctis (formerly UK NARIC) as being equivalent - a UK bachelor’s degree, master’s degree, or PhD
You also satisfy the English language requirement if you met one of these two points in a previous successful visa application.

Who Does Not Need - Prove Their Knowledge of English

You will not need - prove your knowledge of English if you’re a national of one of the following countries or terri-ries:

Antigua and Barbuda
Australia
the Bahamas
Barbados
Belize
the British overseas terri-ries
Canada
Dominica
Grenada
Guyana
Jamaica
Malta
New Zealand
St Kitts and Nevis
St Lucia
St Vincent and the Grenadines
Trinidad and -bago
USA
7. Your Employment Rights

When you work in the UK your employer must:

pay you an agreed rate, which must be at least the national minimum wage
not force you - work excessive hours
give you agreed holiday pay
give you the notice you’re entitled - if your employment ends
You should already have agreed your employment conditions with your employer and have a copy of these in writing. Your employer cannot change your employment conditions unless you agree.

If your employer does not meet these requirements, you can take legal action through an employment or industrial tribunal or the civil courts.

Get Advice and Support

You can get free and confidential advice from the Acas helpline.

You can also contact the charity Kalayaan for free, confidential, and independent advice as a domestic worker in the UK.

If You Want - Return Home

Contact your country’s Embassy or High Commission in the UK if you want - return home.

You can also get confidential advice from a registered immigration adviser. Use the Office of the Immigration Services Commissioner (OISC) Adviser Finder - find a registered adviser near you.

8. If You’re a Victim of Modern Slavery or Human Trafficking

Modern slavery and human trafficking involve being forced - do something you do not want - do, usually by being hurt or threatened.

You may be forced - work for free or less than the minimum wage, get married, or move - a country against your will.

You can apply - stay in the UK for up - 2 years if both of the following apply:

you have a ‘conclusive grounds’ letter from the Single Competent Authority (SCA) confirming that you’re a victim of modern slavery or human trafficking
you entered the UK on an Overseas Domestic Worker visa, on a Domestic Worker in a Private Household visa, or as a private servant of a diplomat (known as a Temporary Work - International Agreement visa).
The Temporary Work - International Agreement visa has now replaced the Temporary Worker – International Agreement Worker visa (T5)

How - Get a Conclusive Grounds Letter

If you think you’re a victim of modern slavery or human trafficking you need - contact the police or another first responder organization. They can help refer your case - the SCA.

Read the ‘First responder organizations’ section of the guidance on referrals - find out which organizations can refer your case.

The SCA will decide if you’re a victim of modern slavery or human trafficking. They will send you a conclusive grounds letter confirming their decision.

Apply

You must apply within 28 days of getting confirmation you’re a victim of modern slavery or human trafficking.

You must apply online - stay in the UK.

It’s free - apply.

Get Help Using a Computer - Apply Online

You can get help with:

accessing a computer or the internet
finding the right information on GOV.UK
You cannot get advice on:

whether you’re eligible - apply
what information - put in your application
an application you’ve already made
Telephone: 03333 445 675, Monday - Friday, 9 am - 5 pm

Text: ‘VISA’ - 07537 416 944, visa@we-are-digital.co.uk

Applying for a Different Visa

If you apply for a different type of visa within 28 days of getting confirmation but are refused, you can still apply as a victim of modern slavery or human trafficking.

You must do this within 28 days of getting the refusal.

Working in the UK

You’ll be able - work as a domestic worker for up - 2 years.

You do not need - have a job offer before you apply. You can change jobs while you’re in the UK.

description:
**Graduate Trainee Visa (Global Business Mobility)**

*Printable version*

**1. Overview**

A Graduate Trainee visa enables you - work for your employer in their UK branch, specifically as part of a graduate training programme for a managerial or specialist role. This visa has replaced the Intra-company Graduate Trainee visa, previously known as Tier 2 (Intra-company Transfer) Graduate Trainee visa. If you're not on a graduate training programme, you might still be eligible - work for your employer's UK branch with a Senior or Specialist Worker visa.

**Eligibility**

- qualify for a Graduate Trainee visa, you must:

- Be an existing employee of an organization approved by the Home Office as a sponsor.
- Have worked for your sponsor outside the UK for at least 3 months immediately before applying.
- Possess a 'certificate of sponsorship' from your employer, outlining details of the work in the UK.
- Engage in a job listed under eligible occupations.
- Receive a salary of at least EUR24,220 per year.

Note: Switching - a Graduate Trainee visa from inside the UK is not permitted.

# Apply - the EU Settlement Scheme (Settled and Pre-Settled Status)

## Overview

The EU Settlement Scheme enables EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, or Liechtenstein citizens and their families, including eligible persons of Northern Ireland, - continue living in the UK. While the deadline was 30 June 2021 for most, applications remain open under specific conditions, such as applying for settled status from pre-settled status or having reasonable grounds for a late application.

### Eligibility:

- Lived in the UK by 31 December 2020
- Meet certain conditions for a later deadline or have reasonable grounds for late application
- Special provisions for Irish citizens and those with indefinite leave - remain

Successful applicants will receive either settled or pre-settled status, allowing for residency, work, and access - public services in the UK.

## Application Process

Applications must be submitted online. For those converting from pre-settled - settled status, the process is free, and certain periods of absence from the UK are permitted under specific conditions.

### Who Can Apply:

- Individuals who lived in the UK by 31 December 2020
- Family members joining eligible UK residents
- Individuals with pre-settled status applying for settled status

### Criteria for Late Applications:

- Joining a family member who was in the UK by 31 December 2020
- Reasonable grounds for not applying by the initial deadline

## Protecting Your Rights

Applying and obtaining a certificate of application ensures the protection of your rights in the UK, including working, renting, and accessing NHS services.

## Fees

There is no fee - apply - the EU Settlement Scheme.

## Settled vs. Pre-Settled Status

- **Settled Status:** Granted usually after 5 years of continuous residence, conferring permanent right - live, work, and access public services in the UK. Eligible for British citizenship after 12 months with settled status.
- **Pre-Settled Status:** For those who haven't lived in the UK for 5 years continuously. Allows stay until eligible for settled status.

## Rights and Travel

Both statuses allow work, education, public funds access (if eligible), and travel in and out of the UK. Time spent outside the UK affects status, with specific limits for settled (up - 5 years) and pre-settled status (up - 2 years).

## Application Documentation

Applicants need valid ID, proof of continuous residence, and evidence of family relationships if applying as a family member. Details vary based on individual circumstances, including applying from within or outside the UK.

## Applying for Children and Family Members

Separate applications are required for each child and family member, with eligibility based on their relationship and the applicant's status. Special conditions apply - Swiss citizens and family members of Northern Ireland.

## After Applying

Applicants receive a certificate of application protecting their rights until a decision is made. Successful applicants get digital confirmation of their status, which is required for employment, renting, and other legal purposes.

## Indefinite Leave and Citizenship

Those with indefinite leave - remain or enter do not need - apply but may choose - for extended travel rights. Settled status holders are generally eligible for British citizenship after 12 months.

This guide provides a comprehensive overview of applying - the EU Settlement Scheme, ensuring EU, EEA, and Swiss citizens and their families can continue - live and work in the UK post-Brexit.

# Frontier Worker Permit

## Overview

The Frontier Worker permit is designed for individuals who work in the UK but reside in another country. It is applicable - citizens from the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, or Liechtenstein who began working in the UK by 31 December 2020 and continue - work in the UK at least once every 12 months. Irish citizens are not required - apply but have the option - do so. British citizens, including those with dual citizenship, are not eligible - apply. Individuals who did not work in the UK by the specified date and wish - work in the UK from 1 January 2021 must apply for a visa.

### Key Features:
- **Eligibility:** EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, or Liechtenstein citizens living outside the UK who started working in the UK by 31 December 2020.
- **Benefits:** Entry - the UK as a frontier worker, access - certain benefits and services, and proof of the right - work or rent in the UK.
- **Fees:** No application fee or immigration health surcharge, though costs may arise for submitting biometric information.

## How - Apply

Applications must be made online, with potential additional steps such as attending an appointment at a visa application centre or UKVCAS service point, depending on the applicant's ability - use the smartphone app for identity verification.

### Required Documents:
- Valid passport or national identity card.
- Employment contracts or proof of self-employment in the UK.
- Evidence of retained worker or self-employed status, if applicable.

## After Applying

If the application is successful, the applicant will receive a digital or physical permit valid for 5 years, or 2 years if applied with 'retained' status. The permit allows for tax obligations in the UK, changing jobs, or moving between employed and self-employed status without notifying the Home Office.

## Renewing Your Permit

- renew the permit, applicants must demonstrate ongoing eligibility, including continued work in the UK or 'retained' status due - temporary inability - work. Renewal applications must also be submitted online.

## Important Notes:
- Family members are not covered by the Frontier Worker permit but may be eligible for the EU Settlement Scheme.
- Living outside the UK primarily is a requirement, with specific criteria for determining eligibility based on time spent in the UK since 1 January 2020.
- Applicants may still qualify during periods of unemployment or inability - work under certain conditions.
- Assistance and inquiries regarding the permit, including reporting issues, can be made through designated contact numbers for applicants inside and outside the UK, as well as organizations assisting with applications.

This permit is essential for eligible workers seeking - maintain their employment in the UK while living abroad, providing them with necessary rights and access - services within the UK.

visaType - countryName: Residence visa for family members - United Arab Emirates
description:
Sponsorship requirements
Expatriate residents can sponsor their families - reside in the UAE if they have a valid residence permit/visa.

 

The sponsor must have a minimum salary of AED 4,000 or AED 3,000 plus accommodation.

Male and female family members who are - be sponsored and who have completed the age of 18 need - undergo and pass medical fitness tests at approved health centres (PDF, 1 MB) in the UAE.

 

Notes:

A mother can sponsor her children in special cases approved by the ICP.
A resident sponsor has 60 days - apply for his dependents? residence visa after they enter the UAE under an entry permit.
A resident can sponsor his parents, and the residence visa will be granted on a yearly basis regardless of the duration of the sponsor?s visa.
The type of profession is no longer a condition for an expatriate worker - be able - sponsor his family visas.
Medically unfit people will not be granted a residence visa.
Residents who are detected with dormant or inactive pulmonary tuberculosis are also considered medically fit and are granted a one-year ?Health Fitness Certificate for Residence? subject - treatment and follow-up by the respective health authority.
 

The conditions are subject - change from time - time. Kindly check with Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship (ICP) or GDRFA.

 

Locate government medical fitness centres of:

Disease Prevention & Screening Center - Abu Dhabi
Dubai Health Authority
Ministry of Health and Prevention.
 

Useful links:

Health conditions for a UAE residence visa - UAE Government portal
Resolution No. 5 of 2016 amending provisions of the Cabinet Decree No. 7 of 2008
Communicable Diseases Bulletin (PDF, 2.65 MB) - Department of Health ? Abu Dhabi
 

Sponsoring your wife and children
An expatriate resident may sponsor the residence visa for his wife and children if he fulfils the above mentioned sponsorship requirements.

 

- sponsor the wife, the expatriate resident must prove an existing marital relationship by submitting an attested marriage certificate in Arabic or duly translated in- Arabic by a certified transla-r.

 

Sponsoring two wives

In strict cases, a Muslim resident may be allowed - sponsor his two wives, if he meets certain terms and conditions set by ICP.

Sponsoring daughters

An expatriate resident can sponsor his daughter/s only if she/they is/are unmarried, with no restrictions with regard - her/their age/s.

 

Sponsoring sons

A male or female resident can sponsor his/her son/s until he is 25. Sons of determination (those with special needs) can be sponsored with no restrictions with regard - his/ their age/s.

 

Sponsoring newborns

For babies born in the UAE, a residence visa must be applied for, within 120 days of its birth - avoid getting fines. 

 

Sponsoring stepchildren

An expatriate resident can sponsor his stepchildren, subject - GDRFA?s conditions which include a deposit for each child and a written no-objection certificate from the biological parent. Their residence visas are valid for one year; renewable annually.

 

Documents required - sponsor wife and children include:

application form - either online or through a registered typing office
passport copies of the wife and children
pho-s of the wife and children
medical clearance certificate of the wife and children above 18 years
copy of the husband's employment contract or company contract
salary certificate from the employer stating the husband?s monthly salary
attested marriage certificate
registered tenancy contract.
 

Cancellation

The family's residence permits are linked - the residence permit of the sponsoring family member . If the sponsoring family member's visa is cancelled, it requires cancellation of the visas of the dependents.

 

Dependents are granted a 6-month grace period from the date of expiry or cancellation of their visas - obtain a new residence permit. If the sponsor fails - renew or cancel the visa of his dependents, he could be liable - pay a fine.

Sponsoring your parents
An expatriate employee can sponsor his parents for a year's stay by paying a deposit as a guarantee for each parent as stipulated by the respective immigration department.

 

An expatriate employee cannot sponsor only one of his parents. He needs - sponsor both parents -gether. He also needs - provide proof that he is their sole support and that there is no one - take care of them back home.

 

If one of the parents has passed away or if the parents are divorced, related official documents would be needed as justification - sponsor only one of the parents. 

 

- sponsor parents, the employed expatriate resident must earn the minimum salary stipulated and obtain a medical insurance policy for parents with the minimum coverage stipulated for each, - be renewed each year.

 

According - the Amer website, DNRD in Dubai stipulates a minimum salary of AED 20,000 - sponsor parents? visa.

 

Residence visa for a UAE citizen spouse parent and child
A UAE citizen?s spouse, parent or child, who holds a foreign passport, can get a UAE residence visa for 5 years without having - work in the UAE. In this case, the sponsor shall be the UAE citizen.

 

A foreign widow or divorced woman, who is a mother of a UAE citizen, can get a residence visa without having - work in the UAE. In this case, the sponsor shall be the oldest child.

 

Source: The Executive Regulation of the Law No. 29 of 2021 on Entry and Residence of Foreigners (PDF, 500 KB).

Updated on 18 Oct 2023

visaType: Residence visa for studying in the UAE
visaType - countryName: Residence visa for studying in the UAE - United Arab Emirates
description:
Student visa
A student can stay in the UAE for studying, either under the sponsorship of his/her parent, who should be a resident of the UAE or under the sponsorship of the accredited university/college he/she is studying at.

Student Affairs offices at universities will facilitate the process - assist students with their visas.

 

A student visa is given for a duration of one year, at a time, renewable for a similar period upon proof of continuation of a study issued by the educational institute where the student is studying.

 

Expatriate residents can sponsor their male child/children up - the age of 25.

 

Therefore, male students over the age of 25 can stay on their parents? sponsorship if they provide evidence of attending a higher educational institute for a minimum of one year?s course. Expatriate residents may continue - sponsor their female children for study, regardless of their age, until she is married.

 

Key requirements

- apply for a student visa, you must submit:

a certificate issued by the university or institute specifying the duration of the study
other general requirements stated in the general provisions for the residence visa.
